title: The caller's active sessions are enumerable, revocable one at a time, and revocable in bulk-except-current
description: The blueprint contributes the `sessionInventory` capability through the session verifier: an authenticated caller can list their active Clerk sessions, revoke one non-current session by id, and revoke every active session except the one being used to make the call. Each list row carries `{ sessionId, deviceLabel, lastActive, currentSession }`; the current session is the one whose id matches the caller's active `__session` cookie. Every operation refuses an unauthenticated caller with a stable-coded `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNAUTHENTICATED` error and no side effect. A revoke against an unknown or already-revoked session id refuses with `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNKNOWN_SESSION` and no side effect. Every operation emits one structured audit event carrying operation, session id prefix and wall-clock timestamp; no field carries a cookie value or a full session id. The consumer contract in `application-account-settings` TAC-2604 reads this interface verbatim.
rationale: The capability declaration on `blueprint.json:capabilities[]` promises consumer blueprints a session-management surface the applying agent can bind against. Without a REQ describing list, revoke-one and revoke-all-except-current, a consumer that gates on `sessionInventory` will render an inventory screen against a contract the provider blueprint never wrote down, and no chain link will fail when the surface returns empty or the revoke is a no-op.
